blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Good to know about Whonnock

items.t: An earlier research pass read the January corridor meeting differently — and the corridor does not reach here in any reading. The City's February 4, 2026 news release and Engage Maple Ridge both state Council approved the Lougheed Transit Corridor OCP amendments on January 27, 2026, with OCP Amending Bylaw No. The corridor ends at 221 Street in the Town Centre — far west of Whonnock — so no transit-corridor density story attaches to a Whonnock acreage.

"Whonnock" is filed twice on this site, by design. It is its own sub-area with its own page, and it is also inside the Northeast page's working scope — a search that runs under only one name can miss listings filed under the other, and neither scope is a City-published boundary.
The nearest condo stock is a different sub-area's stock.

School bus eligibility is a listed-school question here. SD42's transportation page lists regular bus service for specific schools, and Whonnock Elementary, Webster's Corners Elementary and Garibaldi Secondary are all listed — in a sub-area with no recreation centre, library branch or shopping centre of its own, bus eligibility and the drive west to Town Centre services are real daily-life line items to confirm by address.

Zone minimums are not subdivision promises. A-2 at 4.0 ha and A-3 at 8.0 ha only matter if the parcel can actually be subdivided, and on ALR land the ALR Use Regulation governs residences — check ALR status before valuing any "potential" in a Whonnock listing.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Whonnock

items.t: Form B diligence (the frame, if a strata townhouse ever trades here): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. No Whonnock complex exists in for this to attach to today; the frame is stated so a future listing is diligenced correctly rather than assumed fee-simple.

: the stock that does exist here is fee-simple acreage housing, which carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees; municipal rules (Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019), ALR rules where they apply, and any registered covenants govern instead. A buyer importing strata expectations onto a Whonnock acreage — or strata fees onto a hypothetical fee-simple townhouse — is applying the wrong frame in both directions.

Suites, SSMUH and ALR: one secondary suite per lot in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3, contained within the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not within the floodplain area; eligible single-detached and duplex lots may have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws. On ALR parcels the provincial ALR Use Regulation also governs: one secondary suite in the principal residence (s. 31) and an additional residence only if the s. 32 conditions are met. ALR status is per-parcel on ALC mapping; wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database; onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation (setbacks including 30 m from a well unless professional advice is obtained).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Whonnock

items.t: Zoning and OCP: The Albion Area Plan (adopted October 28, 2025) does not cover Whonnock.

Lougheed Transit Corridor — adopted position, with the correction stated: cite the corridor as ADOPTED January 27, 2026 per the City record — OCP Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021 received third reading and adoption on January 27, 2026, the City issued a news release on February 4, 2026, and the corridor ends at 221 Street, far west of Whonnock, so it does not designate Whonnock parcels.

Suites and added units, as the City and the ALR Regulation state them: one secondary suite per lot is permitted in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3, contained within the single detached building, to a maximum of 40% of gross floor area, and not in the Floodplain Area. On ALR parcels the provincial ALR Use Regulation also governs: it permits one secondary suite in the principal residence (s.31) and an additional residence only if the s.32 conditions are met.

ALR block — full form (Whonnock's agricultural ground): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s.6; Strata Property Act, s.239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s.21(1)). Residence caps: one principal residence per parcel, maximum 500 m²; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Farm class (BC Assessment) in full three-tier form: $2,500 of gross farm income at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" statement is an ERROR; none is documented on this area's page in its research, so no page defect is asserted on that point.

Property transfer tax — worked anchors for acreage pricing: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2,000,000, 3% above $2,000,000, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000. First-time buyers' and newly built home exemptions are HOME exemptions — a bare lot's eligibility is UNCONFIRMED here.

items.t: The transit corridor stops well short of Whonnock. The Lougheed Transit Corridor (adopted January 27, 2026) ends at 221 Street in the Town Centre — a Whonnock parcel carries no corridor density story, and route 701's east trips mostly end at 248 Street, short of Whonnock as well.

A Webster's Corners catchment does not transfer east. The one nearby locator result in the research (25554 Dewdney Trunk Road → Webster's Corners Elementary → Garibaldi Secondary) belongs to that address only; Whonnock catchments are UNVERIFIED until the exact address is run.
No official boundary for Whonnock exists in the research — the page's 264 St–288 St scope is a working description only.

faq.a: One secondary suite per lot is permitted in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3 if it sits inside the single detached building, is at most 40% of gross floor area and is not in the Floodplain Area; on ALR land the ALR Use Regulation also applies, and an additional separate residence is allowed only under its s. 32 conditions.

faq.q: Is there a 55+ townhouse or condo in Whonnock?
faq.a: None verified of any form — and the trap to avoid is Haney Pioneer Village: it is a 60+ co-operative in Haney, not in Whonnock, not strata, and not 55+. A Whonnock search that surfaces it has left the sub-area and changed tenure at the same time. (Standing corrections, 2026-11-01.)
